name: Popup
purpose: Anchor a floating, dismissible panel of arbitrary content to a trigger element.
intent: Give components that need a positioned, dismissible floating panel (Tooltip, Inline Message, Dropdown Menu, ...) a shared primitive instead of each hand-rolling their own viewport-aware positioning and Escape/outside-click handling.

figmaSource.structure: Two component properties beyond the variant axes: an exposed SLOT (the anchor/trigger region) and an internal, unpromoted Slot inside the nested `figma-parts / popup` panel instance (the content region). Code models this as `children` (trigger) + `content` (panel content) rather than two Figma-shaped slot props, since the inner slot was never promoted to the outer component set's own property list.
apiAdaptationNotes: Figma's `isOpen` variant became the `open` prop, not `isOpen` - `open` is a native HTML attribute (dialog/details), and component-api-governance.json prefers native names whenever one exists.

`alignment`'s default (`topLeft`) matches Figma's own declared default variant exactly, even though a click-opened floating panel more typically opens below its trigger - there was no product signal in the source file to justify overriding it.

Dismissal (Escape/outside click) has no Figma variant at all - it's a code-level behavior decision, not a design-source fact. Added as opt-out (default on) rather than opt-in, so most consumers get it for free.

padding gained a fourth value, `none`, on 2026-08-19 when Dropdown Menu was built on top of Popup: its Figma instance of `popup` wraps a `menu` panel with zero outer padding around it (the menu's own search field and rows already carry their own insets, matching the padding=0 measured directly on the dropdown-menu component's nested panelSurface/content/menu node chain). `sm`/`md`/`lg` were insufficient for this real consumer, so the enum grew rather than having Dropdown Menu reach for `unstyled` and re-declare background/border/radius/shadow itself.

useCases: Foundation for a click-to-open action menu anchored to a button
Foundation for a short confirmation or status message anchored to the action that triggered it
Any future component needing a positioned, dismissible floating panel
Foundation for a hover-triggered, non-interactive hint with its own visual skin and dismissal semantics (Tooltip, via `unstyled` and `manageTriggerAria={false}`)
antiPatterns: Using Popup directly as a user-facing component - it has no visual identity of its own
Content essential to task completion that the user can't afford to have scroll out of view

anatomy.description: The single trigger element. Cloned to receive a measurement ref, and (unless manageTriggerAria is false) aria-expanded/aria-controls - Popup attaches no open/close event handlers to it.
The floating, position: fixed panel. Rendered only while `open` is true.
Arbitrary, potentially interactive content rendered inside the panel.

children.description: The single trigger element to clone and attach a measurement ref and aria attributes to.

content.description: Rendered inside the floating panel while open is true.

open.description: Controlled visibility. Popup has no internal open state and no defaultOpen.

onOpenChange.description: Called with false on Escape or an outside click. Popup does not change its own visibility.

alignment.description: Preferred side/edge alignment. Falls back to whichever of the six overflows the viewport least.

closeOnOutsideClick.description: Calls onOpenChange(false) on a pointer press outside the trigger and panel.

id.description: Id applied to the panel and to the trigger's aria-controls while open. Generated via React.useId when omitted.

role.description: ARIA role for the panel. No default - depends on what the consumer is building.

className.description: Composes with the panel's class list.

unstyled.description: Skips Popup's own visual skin (background, border, padding, radius, shadow), leaving only structural positioning and the mount animation. Set this when a consumer has an entirely different visual design of its own - e.g. Tooltip.

padding.description: Padding for Popup's own visual skin, mapped to the spacing scale (none=0, sm=--spacing-sm, md=--spacing-md, lg=--spacing-lg). Lets a consumer size the skin (e.g. a menu's denser rows, or a consumer whose own content manages all edge padding) while still sharing background/border/radius/shadow. Ignored when unstyled is true.

manageTriggerAria.description: Sets aria-expanded/aria-controls on the trigger while true. Set to false when the consumer already manages the trigger's own ARIA relationship to the panel content (e.g. Tooltip's aria-describedby) - aria-expanded/aria-controls are disclosure-widget attributes and don't apply to a supplemental hint.

anchorRef.description: Element to measure for positioning, width-matching, and the outside-click boundary, instead of the cloned trigger child. Use when the child carrying the merged ref + aria-expanded is smaller than the visible control it lives inside - e.g. Select's trigger is a text input (where the ARIA belongs) inset within a bordered field frame, and the panel should align to and match the frame. The trigger child still receives the merged ref and ARIA; only measurement and the dismissal boundary follow this element. Falls back to the trigger child.

matchTriggerWidth.description: Sizes the panel to the measured trigger (the anchorRef element, or the trigger child) rather than letting it hug its own content - so a field's dropdown matches the field's width. The consumer's panel content must be able to fill that width (Dropdown Menu passes `fullWidth` to its Menu for exactly this).

topLeft.purpose: Opens above the trigger, left edges aligned.

topRight.purpose: Opens above the trigger, right edges aligned.

topCenter.purpose: Opens above the trigger, horizontally centered on it.

bottomLeft.purpose: Opens below the trigger, left edges aligned.

bottomRight.purpose: Opens below the trigger, right edges aligned.

bottomCenter.purpose: Opens below the trigger, horizontally centered on it.

none.purpose: Zero padding - the consumer's own content manages all edge padding (e.g. Dropdown Menu's Menu panel, whose search field and rows already carry their own insets).

sm.purpose: Denser skin padding (--spacing-sm) - e.g. a menu's rows.

lg.purpose: Default skin padding (--spacing-lg), matching Figma's popup component.

tokens.note: --color-elevation-shadow-overlay-spread and -perimeter were added alongside this component - they mirror the existing --color-elevation-shadow-raised-* family's shape, using the exact alpha values (16%, 32%) read from Figma's Light/elevation.shadow.overlay effect style. The dark-theme values mirror elevation.shadow.raised's light-to-dark base-hue swap at the same percentages rather than an independently re-verified dark effect.

triggeredBy: consumer-controlled - Popup attaches no open/close handler itself
accessibility.ariaExpanded: set on the trigger, reflecting open, unless manageTriggerAria is false
accessibility.ariaControls: set on the trigger to the panel id only while open, unless manageTriggerAria is false; preserves an existing value while closed
accessibility.focusManagement: left to the consumer - Popup does not move focus into or out of the panel
requirements: aria-expanded reflects open on the trigger by default (manageTriggerAria=true).
aria-controls points at the panel id only while open, by default.
manageTriggerAria=false skips both attributes entirely, for consumers with their own trigger ARIA relationship (e.g. aria-describedby).
No default role is added to the panel - the consumer supplies one appropriate to its content.
Popup does not make the trigger focusable or change its semantics beyond the two aria attributes above.

keyboardInteraction: Escape calls onOpenChange(false) when closeOnEscape is true (default).
No other keyboard behavior is owned by Popup - content-specific navigation (e.g. arrow keys in a menu) belongs to the consumer.
behaviorRules: open is a required, fully controlled prop - no internal open state, no defaultOpen.
Popup never changes its own visibility on dismissal - it only calls onOpenChange(false).
Clones the trigger to attach a measurement ref, and (unless manageTriggerAria is false) aria-expanded/aria-controls; attaches no click/hover handlers.
Positions via a portal at document.body with position: fixed, recalculating on trigger/panel resize, window resize, and scroll.
Tries the preferred alignment first, then the same alignment on the opposite side, then the remaining four, and resolves to whichever overflows the viewport least, exposed via data-alignment.
Escape (document keydown) and outside pointer press (document pointerdown, capture phase) both gate on their respective closeOn* prop before calling onOpenChange.
A pointer press inside the panel or on the trigger itself never triggers outside-click dismissal.
Renders nothing but the cloned trigger when open is false - no empty portal node stays mounted.

unstyled=true omits Popup's own visual skin class (and the padding class) from the panel entirely, leaving only structural positioning and the mount animation - the base .panel class never carries visual styling, so there's no cross-module CSS override needed.

padding selects one of four dedicated classes (padding_none/sm/md/lg), kept separate from panelSurface's other properties (background/border/radius/shadow/gap) so a consumer can size the skin without needing to override or duplicate the rest of it.

When the trigger scrolls fully out of the viewport (all four edges checked - top/bottom/left/right), the panel is hidden (visibility: hidden, data-trigger-out-of-view="true") rather than clamped to the nearest viewport edge - clamping left it visibly stuck at that edge with no visible anchor once the trigger was no longer on screen at all. Resumes normal positioning automatically once the trigger scrolls back into view (even partially). Gated on the trigger having a measured, nonzero size, so an unlaid-out element (e.g. a test that doesn't mock layout) is never treated as out of view.
compositionRules: Consumers own trigger interaction entirely - wire the trigger's own onClick (or other handler) to flip the open state passed into Popup.
Provide onOpenChange whenever closeOnEscape or closeOnOutsideClick are left at their default true - otherwise dismissal has no visible effect.
Pass role matching what's being built on top of Popup (menu, dialog, status, ...) - Popup does not infer one.
Set unstyled when the consumer supplies its own complete visual design (background, border, padding, radius, shadow) via className, rather than fighting Popup's default skin with CSS overrides.
Prefer padding over unstyled when only the padding needs to differ - it keeps background/border/radius/shadow shared from one source instead of duplicating those token references per consumer.

Set manageTriggerAria={false} when the consumer already manages the trigger's ARIA relationship to the panel (e.g. aria-describedby for a hint) - Popup's aria-expanded/aria-controls are for disclosure widgets specifically.
contentRules: content may be any React.ReactNode, including interactive elements - unlike Tooltip, Popup content is not restricted to non-interactive material.
responsiveRules: Positioning recalculates on resize/scroll identically across breakpoints.
Outside-click dismissal uses pointerdown, which fires for touch as well as mouse/pen.
themeRules: All panel tokens (background, border, shadow) resolve correctly on both light and dark surfaces via the semantic color layer - no component-level light/dark branching.
implementationNotes: Use React.memo for the exported component.
No hardcoded colors, spacing, or radius - use the tokens listed above.

Popup is now the shared floating-position implementation - Tooltip renders through it (unstyled, alignment=topCenter) rather than maintaining its own local positioning/portal code, which it did before Popup existed.
do: Keep open state in the consumer and pass it down.
Provide onOpenChange when relying on default dismissal behavior.
Pass role matching the content being built on top of Popup.
Turn off closeOnEscape/closeOnOutsideClick for content that must persist until the consumer explicitly closes it.
dont: Do not expect Popup to manage its own open state.
Do not use Popup for non-interactive hover hints - use Tooltip.
Do not rely on Popup to move focus into or out of the panel.
Do not attach open/close handlers to the trigger expecting Popup to call them - Popup only clones ref and aria attributes onto it.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders only the cloned trigger when open is false.
Renders content inside a portal panel when open is true.
Sets aria-expanded/aria-controls on the trigger reflecting open, unless manageTriggerAria is false.
Applies the requested role to the panel; no role by default.
Calls onOpenChange(false) on Escape when closeOnEscape is true (default).
Calls onOpenChange(false) on an outside pointer press when closeOnOutsideClick is true (default).
Does not call onOpenChange for a pointer press inside the panel or on the trigger.
Resolves to a fitting alignment (preferring the same alignment on the opposite side before an unrelated one) and exposes it via data-alignment.
Supports a custom id and className.
Applies its own visual skin by default; omits it entirely when unstyled is true.
Defaults padding to lg; applies none/sm/md/lg padding classes per the padding prop; applies none when unstyled is true.
Panel styling maps to the required tokens and hugs its content rather than stretching.

Hides the panel (visibility: hidden) once the trigger's bounding rect is fully outside the viewport on any edge, without changing open or clamping to that edge; shows it again, correctly positioned, once the trigger is back in view.
knownLimitations: No built-in focus management - focus trapping/restoration is left entirely to the consumer.
Dark-theme shadow alpha values mirror the elevation.shadow.raised family's percentages rather than an independently re-verified dark Figma effect.
futureEnhancements: Optional built-in focus-trap behavior for consumers that want it without implementing their own.
